subject: history_social
passage: Many medieval cathedrals in Europe took more than a century to finish, and work on them often stopped for years at a time. Historian Claire Moreau argues that these long pauses happened mainly because the people in charge of building ran out of money, not because of wars or other outside events.
stem: Which finding, if true, would most directly weaken Moreau's argument?

choices.A: Building records show that work usually stopped when wars broke out, even while donations kept arriving.
choices.B: Building records show that work usually stopped soon after the money collected for construction was spent.
choices.C: Many medieval cathedrals have stained-glass windows showing stories that were familiar to local people.
choices.D: Some skilled builders traveled from city to city, working on several cathedrals during their careers.

explanation.why: Moreau claims the pauses came mainly from a lack of money rather than from wars. A finding weakens her if it shows work stopping because of war at times when money was still available.
explanation.A: Correct. Work stopped during wars even though donations kept coming in, so a lack of money cannot explain these pauses.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Work stopping when the money ran out fits Moreau's argument, so this would support it.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The windows' subjects say nothing about why construction stopped.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Builders moving between cities does not show what caused the long pauses.
